description: Config-driven SKU sizing and pricing logic for the Node.js migration assessment agent. The agent reads this file, fetches the live SKU catalog and retail prices for the chosen region, then applies these rules to size and price each server's compute and storage. Aligns the agent's methodology with Azure Migrate (as-allocated, 1 disk per source disk, Standard SSD by default).

region._note: Change armRegionName to target a different region, e.g. 'malaysiawest'. Every price lookup and SKU-availability query must be scoped to this region.

rightSizing._note: auto = per-row: use performance-based when CPU/Memory utilization columns are present and valid for that row, else fall back to as-allocated. This matches Azure Migrate behaviour.

performanceBased._note: Industry-standard formula (Azure Migrate aligned): requiredCores = ceil(observedCores * (max(observedCpu%, minimumUtilizationPercent) / 100) * cpuComfortFactor). Same pattern for RAM. Edge-case rules: (1) utilization == 0 OR missing -> fall back to as-allocated for that row (server may have been off / agent broken / measurement window too short - undersizing risk is real). (2) utilization < minimumUtilizationPercent (20%) -> floor to 20% (idle workloads still need baseline capacity to handle bursts and OS overhead). (3) utilization > 100% -> cap at 100% (measurement quirk). Percentile (95th) is taken from the source telemetry by Azure Migrate; this agent uses whatever single value the inventory provides as already representing that percentile.

industryOptimized._note: Conservative right-sizing for inventories with NO performance telemetry. Industry rule-of-thumb (Gartner / Microsoft FastTrack): on-prem VMs typically run at 25-35% CPU utilisation, so multiplying allocated cores by 0.7 leaves the Azure VM at ~50% utilisation if the workload behaves as expected on-prem. RAM tends to be less oversized (apps grab and hold) so 0.8 is the safer default. Floors at compute.minimums.vCPUs / memoryGB. Both factors are user-editable in the UI.

keepWhere._note: Drop any SKU whose restrictions array is non-empty for the target region (NotAvailableForSubscription / location). Read vCPUs and MemoryGB from the capabilities array.

familySelection._note: ratio = requiredRamGB / requiredCores. Walk rules top-down; first rule whose maxRamPerCore >= ratio wins. families are tried in listed priority order during SKU matching.

selectionAlgorithm.fallback: If no SKU in the selected family list satisfies both constraints, advance to the next family in the rule; if all listed families fail, search the entire region catalog for the cheapest SKU meeting both constraints and flag the row as 'family-fallback'.

pricing.queryFilter: serviceName eq 'Virtual Machines' and armRegionName eq '{armRegionName}' and priceType eq 'Consumption'
pricing._pricingNote: Use the LINUX base rate (retailPrice). Do not use Windows meters; handle Windows licensing via Azure Hybrid Benefit separately. Exclude Spot / Low Priority. There is usually one Consumption Linux hourly meter per armSkuName per region.

azureHybridBenefit._note: Capture AHB savings as a separate line, do not bake into base compute. Azure Migrate reports it in its own column. Only apply when the customer confirms Software Assurance / RHEL-SUSE cloud subscription eligibility.

storage._diskTypeNote: Default StandardSSD to match Azure Migrate for as-allocated, non-performance-sized workloads. Switch to PremiumSSD only for confirmed latency/IOPS-sensitive tiers (e.g. production databases). StandardHDD for cold/archival storage.

diskCounting._note: CRITICAL: emit one priced disk row per source disk. Do NOT collapse multiple disks of a server into a single disk. If a server has 4 data disks, size and price 4 disks.

sizing.rule: Select the smallest tier whose maxGiB >= sourceDiskSizeGB.

oversizeGuard._note: If sourceDiskSizeGB > 32767, split across multiple max-tier disks and sum their prices.

pricing.queryFilter: serviceName eq 'Storage' and armRegionName eq '{armRegionName}' and priceType eq 'Consumption'
pricing._pricingNote: Managed-disk capacity price is already per-month for the WHOLE disk (flat per tier, not per GiB). Take the 'X Disks' / 'X LRS Disk' per-month meter, NOT transaction/IOPS/throughput meters. Match skuName to the selected tier exactly (e.g. 'E15 LRS Disk'). Do not multiply by size — the tier price is the full monthly cost of that disk.

defenderForCloud._note: Azure Migrate adds a security line (~$17.5k/mo on this inventory). Price Defender for Servers per protected server-hour or per server/month from the retail API (serviceName eq 'Microsoft Defender for Cloud') and add it as its own line so the agent total reconciles to Azure Migrate.

options.label: AMD (Recommended)
options.desc: AMD-based SKUs (as_v5, ads_v5) — matches Azure Migrate default

options.label: Automatic (Best Fit)
options.desc: Let sizing logic decide based on cost/availability — no architecture filter

cpuArchitecture._note: AMD SKUs contain 'a' after the size number (e.g., D8as_v5). Intel SKUs do not (e.g., D8s_v5). 'auto' applies no filter. The pattern is matched against the portion after Standard_X<N> in the SKU name.

pricingModels.name: 1-Year Reserved Instance
pricingModels.filter: priceType eq 'Reservation' and reservationTerm eq '1 Year'
pricingModels.label: 1yr RI

pricingModels.name: 3-Year Reserved Instance
pricingModels.filter: priceType eq 'Reservation' and reservationTerm eq '3 Years'
pricingModels.label: 3yr RI

outputContract.reconciliationRule: totalMonthlyCompute MUST equal the sum of every row's monthlyComputePrice; totalMonthlyStorage MUST equal the sum of every disk's monthlyStoragePrice. Assert this in code before writing the summary.
